reasons: narrow: Omission of exact-support, positivity, or all-cell-equality predicates from the definition of the published witness relation does not by itself prove set noninclusion. Noninclusion follows if a published witness violating one of those predicates exists; the proposed statement makes that necessary existence premise explicit.
Remove the unresolved open-ended residual dichotomy from the dependencies and record only the two proved inputs to the narrowed sound partial-decision theorem.

narrow: The asserted equivalence is exactly the unresolved residual dichotomy. The frozen residual token permits finite candidate lists but supplies no exhaustiveness theorem, so a maximal execution can be stuck with no accepted candidate. The proposed claim records the strongest unconditional sound partial-decision theorem and does not assume the missing converse.
REVIEW: result-class degradation — the load-bearing construct (minimax / lower bound / equivalence / iff) is dropped to a surviving fragment (keep the result, mark it open if unproven)
The narrowed theorem uses normalization and the three nonresidual transition definitions, not the unresolved completeness theorem.

narrow: Normalization retains selector provenance and dormant coordinates, so the normalized object is only substantively equivalent to the ordinary expansion after suppressing a deterministic coordinate. Moreover, the residual libraries are not proved to contain every classical hedge certificate; the ordinary semantic and transition reduction is provable, but the complete residual classification is not.

narrow: The frozen transition definitions permit a step-for-step embedding of a successful published derivation, but they do not specify token initialization or prove confluence of the lexicographically greedy schedule. Therefore existence of a valid trace is proved, while the claim that this particular schedule necessarily selects it is not derivable.
Align the statement metadata with the narrowed claim, which proves local transition invariance and well-foundedness but not global progress of token generation.

narrow: Strict descent proves that every admitted execution is finite, but the frozen machine does not prove that all initialized nonresidual tokens pass their eligibility tests. The proposed statement separates well-foundedness and local soundness from the unproved progress and residual-exhaustiveness claims.

verdict.note: Accept the logical witness-separation correction; reject four result-degrading weakenings and keep the formula-or-global-twin contract open on its OEQ. Hand-transcribe the Wald dependency repair separately.
